facts.statement: Mistralazhdarcho lived during the Campanian and Maastrichtian ages of the Late Cretaceous in what is now France.
facts.quote: Mistralazhdarcho is a genus of azhdarchid pterosaur that lived during the Campanian and Maastrichtian ages of the Late Cretaceous period in what is now France.

facts.statement: The holotype was found in the Aix-en-Provence Basin and consists of a partial skeleton including part of the mandible.
facts.quote: They were found in a layer of the Aix-en-Provence Basin at Velaux–La Bastide Neuve and consist of a partial skeleton that includes part of the mandible.

facts.statement: Mistralazhdarcho maggii was named and described in 2018 by Valentin, Vullo, Garcia, Godefroit, and Cincotta.
facts.quote: These remains would later be made the holotype specimen of the new genus and type species Mistralazhdarcho maggii, named and described in 2018 by Valentin, along with paleontologists Romain Vullo, Géraldine Garcia, Pascal Godefroit, and Aude Cincotta.

facts.statement: The genus name Mistralazhdarcho combines the local northern wind 'mistral' with the related genus Azhdarcho.
facts.quote: The generic name combines the mistral, a typical northern wind from the area, and the related genus Azhdarcho.

facts.statement: The species name maggii honors Jean-Pierre Maggi, the mayor of Velaux who supported the paleontological project.
facts.quote: The specific name honors Jean-Pierre Maggi, the mayor of Velaux, who supported the La Bastide Neuve paleontological project.

facts.statement: Extrapolations suggest the holotype wingspan was between 4.24 and 4.85 meters.
facts.quote: Based on extrapolations of the size of its humerus and the wingspan of the related pterosaur Zhejiangopterus, the estimated wingspan for the holotype specimen of Mistralazhdarcho sits between 4.24 and 4.85 m.

facts.statement: Adult individuals are estimated to have had wingspans between 5 and 6 meters, as the holotype was not fully grown.
facts.quote: However, the holotype is not fully grown. Wingspans of adult individuals are estimated to have measured between 5 and 6 m.

facts.statement: Mistralazhdarcho was assigned to the family Azhdarchidae, though no cladistic analysis was performed in its original description.
facts.quote: Mistralazhdarcho was assigned to the family Azhdarchidae by Vullo and colleagues, though a cladistic analysis was not made in its description.

facts.statement: The phylogenetic placement of Mistralazhdarcho varies depending on the study.
facts.quote: Later studies would include Mistralazhdarcho in their phylogenetic analyses, but its placement varies depending on the study.

facts.statement: Some studies place Mistralazhdarcho in the subfamily Azhdarchinae, while others place it in Quetzalcoatlinae.
facts.quote: Within Azhdarchidae, some have recovered Mistralazhdarcho in the subfamily Azhdarchinae, while others in Quetzalcoatlinae.

facts.statement: The fossil layer dates back to the late Campanian, approximately 72 million years ago.
facts.quote: The layer dates back to the late Campanian, about 72 million years ago.

facts.statement: The bones were found on a 5 square meter surface within a 140 square meter fossil layer, suggesting a single individual.
facts.quote: The skeleton was not found articulated but the bones were discovered on a limited surface of 5 m2 within the total surface of 140 m2 formed by the fossil layer.

facts.statement: The remains represent a single individual, likely a subadult.
facts.quote: Therefore, it was concluded they represent a single individual, probably a subadult.

facts.statement: The humerus was estimated to have an original length of 19 centimeters.
facts.quote: The humerus was estimated to have had an original length of 19 cm.

facts.statement: Estimates corroborate the hypothesis that the holotype had a wingspan of about 4.5 meters.
facts.quote: Both estimates seem to corroborate the hypothesis that the holotype individual of Mistralazhdarcho had a wingspan of about 4.5 m.

facts.statement: A unique trait is an elevation on the midline of the lower jaw symphysis located 18 cm behind the tip, compared to 32 cm in Alanqa.
facts.quote: One of these was an autapomorphy, a unique derived character. The upper surface of the symphysis of the lower jaws shows a well-developed elevation on the midline in a relatively forward position of 18 cm behind the mandible tip, compared to 32 cm in the related pterosaur Alanqa.

facts.statement: A 2021 study by Brian Andres recovered Mistralazhdarcho as the sister taxon of Aerotitan in the subfamily Azhdarchinae.
facts.quote: For example, a 2021 study by American paleontologist Brian Andres recovered Mistralazhdarcho as the sister taxon of Aerotitan in the subfamily Azhdarchinae within Azhdarchidae, in the most derived (advanced) position.

facts.statement: Mistralazhdarcho is the first pterosaur named from the Campanian to Maastrichtian of Western Europe.
facts.quote: Mistralazhdarcho is the first pterosaur named from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian of Western Europe.

facts.statement: The fossil site for Mistralazhdarcho was discovered in 1992 by Xavier Valentin in Velaux–La Bastide Neuve, southern France.
facts.quote: En 1992, Xavier Valentin descubrió un rico yacimiento fosilífero en Velaux–La Bastide Neuve, en el sur de Francia.

facts.statement: The species Mistralazhdarcho maggii was named and described in 2018 by Romain Vullo, Géraldine Garcia, Pascal Godefroit, Aude Cincotta, and Xavier Valentin.
facts.quote: La especie tipo Mistralazhdarcho maggii fue nombrada y descrita en 2018 por Romain Vullo, Géraldine Garcia, Pascal Godefroit, Aude Cincotta y Xavier Valentin.

facts.statement: The genus name combines the Mistral wind, typical of the discovery area, with Azhdarcho, the type genus of the family Azhdarchidae.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se refiere al mistral, un viento del norte típico del área del descubrimiento, combinándolo con Azhdarcho, el género tipo de la familia Azhdarchidae.

facts.statement: The species name honors Jean-Pierre Maggi, the mayor of Velaux, for his support of the La Bastide Neuve paleontological project.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie es en honor de Jean-Pierre Maggi, el alcalde de Velaux, por su apoyo al proyecto paleontológico de La Bastide Neuve.

facts.statement: Using a formula by Alexandr Averianov, the wingspan is estimated at 424 centimeters.
facts.quote: Esto indica una envergadura alar de 424 centímetros usando una fórmula ideada por Alexandr Averianov.

facts.statement: Extrapolating from the relatively complete skeleton of Zhejiangopterus yields an estimated wingspan of 485 centimeters.
facts.quote: Otro método consiste en extrapolar la envergadura a partir de un azdárquido con esqueleto relativamente completo, Zhejiangopterus. Esto da como resultado un estimado de 485 centímetros.

facts.statement: Both estimates support the hypothesis that the holotype individual had a wingspan of nearly 4.5 meters.
facts.quote: Ambas estimaciones parecen corroborar la hipótesis de que el individuo del holotipo tenía una envergadura de cerca de 4.5 metros.

facts.statement: A second possible unique trait is a slight downward curvature at the tip of the mandible.
facts.quote: Hay una segunda característica que podría ser una posible autapomorfia, la punta de la mandíbula posee cierta curvatura hacia abajo.

facts.statement: A unique combination of traits includes blunt, elevated crests on the edges of the upper mandibular symphysis surface.
facts.quote: Adicionalmente, se proporcionó una combinación única de rasgos que por sí mismos no son únicos: la superficie superior de la sinfísis mandibular muestra unas crestas elevadas y romas en sus bordes.

facts.statement: The symphysis has a V-shaped cross-section and lacks a lower crest.
facts.quote: La sínfisis posee una sección transversal en forma de letra V, careciendo por tanto de una cresta inferior.

facts.statement: The humerus is relatively short compared to the radius, being only 66% of its length.
facts.quote: El húmero es relativamente corto comparado con el radio, con solo el 66% de su longitud.

facts.statement: Mistralazhdarcho was placed in the family Azhdarchidae in 2018, though without a precise cladistic analysis.
facts.quote: Mistralazhdarcho fue situado en la familia Azhdarchidae en 2018, aunque sin un análisis cladístico preciso.

facts.statement: The shared symphysis elevation suggests a close relationship between Mistralazhdarcho and the genus Alanqa.
facts.quote: La elevación de la sínfisis compartida con Alanqa sugiere una cercana relación entre ambos géneros.

facts.statement: Mistralazhdarcho is the first named pterosaur from the Campanian-Maastrichtian of Western Europe.
facts.quote: Mistralazhdarcho es el primer pterosaurio nombrado del Campaniense-Maastrichtiense de Europa occidental.

facts.statement: The parent group of Mistralazhdarcho is Azhdarchidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Azhdarchidae

facts.statement: Mistralazhdarcho is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The time range for Mistralazhdarcho is the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)
